hints: Use the geometry of the circle: string $AR$ makes $25^\circ$ with the vertical at $A$. Since $CA = CR = r$, $\triangle ACR$ is isosceles and radius $CR$ makes $50^\circ$ with the vertical.
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium: $R\sin 50^\circ = T\sin 25^\circ$.
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium: $T\cos 25^\circ = 40 + R\cos 50^\circ$, and solve the two simultaneous equations for $R$ and $T$.
walkthrough:
Identify the direction of the normal reaction $R$ from the geometry of circle with centre $C$:
In isosceles triangle $ACR$ ($CA = CR = r$), $\angle CAR = 25^\circ$, so $\angle CRA = 25^\circ$.
The angle the radius $CR$ makes with the vertical downward direction is $2 \times 25^\circ = 50^\circ$.

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$R\sin 50^\circ = T\sin 25^\circ$$
$$T = R\frac{\sin 50^\circ}{\sin 25^\circ} = R\frac{2\sin 25^\circ\cos 25^\circ}{\sin 25^\circ} = 2R\cos 25^\circ \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium with ring weight $W = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$:
$$T\cos 25^\circ = 40 + R\cos 50^\circ \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Substitute Equation 1 into Equation 2:
$$(2R\cos 25^\circ)\cos 25^\circ = 40 + R\cos 50^\circ$$
$$2R\cos^2 25^\circ = 40 + R(2\cos^2 25^\circ - 1)$$
$$2R\cos^2 25^\circ = 40 + 2R\cos^2 25^\circ - R \implies R = 40\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Analyze the geometry of the vertical circular wire:
- Center of wire: $C$
- Highest point: $A$, vertical diameter passes through $A$ and $C$
- Ring position: $R$ on the wire
- Radius lines: $CA = CR = r$, forming an isosceles triangle $\triangle ACR$
- Given: string $AR$ makes an angle of $25^\circ$ with the vertical line $AC$, so $\angle CAR = 25^\circ$
- Since $CA = CR$, base angles are equal: $\angle CRA = 25^\circ$
- The angle at the center $\angle ACR = 180^\circ - 2(25^\circ) = 130^\circ$
- Therefore, the radius $CR$ makes an angle of $180^\circ - 130^\circ = 50^\circ$ with the downward vertical.

Identify the three coplanar forces acting on the ring at $R$:
- Tension $T$ in string $AR$, directed along $RA$ at an angle of $25^\circ$ to the upward vertical.
- Weight $W = mg = (4)(10) = 40\text{ N}$ directed vertically downwards.
- Normal reaction $R_{\text{normal}}$ from the smooth wire, directed radially outwards along $CR$, making an angle of $50^\circ$ to the downward vertical.

Set up horizontal equilibrium:
$$\sum F_x = 0$$
$$R_{\text{normal}}\sin 50^\circ - T\sin 25^\circ = 0$$
$$T\sin 25^\circ = R_{\text{normal}}\sin 50^\circ$$
Using the double-angle identity $\sin 50^\circ = 2\sin 25^\circ\cos 25^\circ$:
$$T\sin 25^\circ = R_{\text{normal}}(2\sin 25^\circ\cos 25^\circ)$$
Divide through by $\sin 25^\circ$:
$$T = 2 R_{\text{normal}}\cos 25^\circ \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Set up vertical equilibrium:
$$\sum F_y = 0$$
$$T\cos 25^\circ - 40 - R_{\text{normal}}\cos 50^\circ = 0$$
$$T\cos 25^\circ = 40 + R_{\text{normal}}\cos 50^\circ \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Substitute Equation 1 into Equation 2:
$$(2 R_{\text{normal}}\cos 25^\circ)\cos 25^\circ = 40 + R_{\text{normal}}\cos 50^\circ$$
$$2 R_{\text{normal}}\cos^2 25^\circ = 40 + R_{\text{normal}}(2\cos^2 25^\circ - 1)$$
$$2 R_{\text{normal}}\cos^2 25^\circ = 40 + 2 R_{\text{normal}}\cos^2 25^\circ - R_{\text{normal}}$$
Subtract $2 R_{\text{normal}}\cos^2 25^\circ$ from both sides:
$$0 = 40 - R_{\text{normal}} \implies R_{\text{normal}} = 40\text{ N}$$

Compute the tension $T$:
$$T = 2(40)\cos 25^\circ = 80\cos 25^\circ$$
$$\cos 25^\circ \approx 0.906308$$
$$T \approx 80 \times 0.906308 = 72.5046\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 72.5\text{ N}$.
Thus, the tension in the string is $72.5\text{ N}$ and the normal reaction of the wire on the ring is $40\text{ N}$.
